title: POC Weekly Sync - Onboarding & Env Readiness
summary: Weekly POC sync to review onboarding progress. Customer completed initial infra prep but had two blockers (VPC peering and KMS access). Redwood SE validated first-run inference tests; latency ~180ms p50 on small test set, token cost higher than expected due to small batch sizes. Agreed to run full benchmark next week after access granted; Redwood to share SOC2 + security docs and a tuning checklist.
action_items: Mark Liu - Create VPC peering request and share peering ID with Redwood by 2026-10-22
Sophie Turner - Provide 500 sample prompts and 10k anonymized records for benchmark by 2026-10-23
Luis Martinez - Send security pack (SOC2, ISO docs), infra checklist, and initial pricing estimate by 2026-10-21
Priya Desai - Run extended benchmark (throughput + latency) once peering & KMS are in place, target complete by 2026-10-28
next_steps: Luis to email security docs + onboarding checklist (link to drive)
Customer to open KMS IAM ticket with cloud team and confirm key alias
Follow-up sync one week after benchmark to review tuning results
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-20
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Luis Martinez (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Hannah Cole (Redwood CSM), Aisha Khan (NexaHealth CTO), Mark Liu (Nexa DevOps), Sophie Turner (Nexa ML Eng), Tom Reyes (Nexa PM)

Summary: quick POC check-in; focus on environment readiness and running a full benchmark next week. A couple of infra blockers but close to resolved.

[00:00] Luis Martinez: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll keep this tight 45 minutes, agenda is quick onboarding check, review the smoke test results and plan the full benchmark.
[00:18] Aisha Khan: thanks Luis, yeah we want to make sure the data path and security are solid before the benchmark, we've got compliance windows this quarter so need SOC2 artifacts.
[00:37] Luis Martinez: absolutely we'll send SOC2 and infra checklist after the call, Priya can you remind folks what you ran for the smoke tests?
[00:45] Priya Desai: yeah so we ran three workloads: short prompt generation, multi-turn chat emulation and embeddings for a small corpus. ran on the dedicated dev cluster you provided credentials for, used a pinned model variant (redwood-1-small) to keep parity. results — p50 latency around 180ms for single-request small prompts, p95 spiked to ~600ms on the odd one, throughput was limited because batching was disabled in the test harness.
[01:12] Sophie Turner: quick q, batching was disabled because of session affinity or because of the harness?
[01:18] Priya Desai: harness - we had the client set to force single inference to measure tail lat, but for the throughput run we'll enable batching and pipeline a token cache.
[01:30] Mark Liu: we've opened the peering request but I didn't include the right CIDR, so that is why your test VM couldn't reach our private endpoint yesterday. i'll fix and re-open.
[01:42] Luis Martinez: ok that's the main blocker then, plus KMS access right? Aisha?
[01:48] Aisha Khan: yes our security team wants Redwood to use our KMS key for customer-controlled key material, we need to confirm IAM roles and key alias.
[01:59] Priya Desai: we support customer-managed keys (CMK) and HSM setups; we just need an IAM role with kms:Decrypt/kms:Encrypt and the key alias. If you share the key ARN and grant Redwood's role we can plug it into the deployment template.
[02:20] Tom Reyes: is there a spreadsheet or a checklist for the exact policies we need to apply? the security team wants text they can throw into a ticket.
[02:28] Luis Martinez: yes we'll include an infra checklist and a sample IAM policy, i'll drop it in the follow-up email.
[02:34] Sophie Turner: about results, the token cost looked higher than our expectations on the initial run — any quick thoughts?
[02:41] Priya Desai: two things: small batch sizes increase per-token overhead, and we were running with no quantization. for the customer workload we usually recommend int8 quant, tuned KV cache, and batching of 4-8 depending on latency SLO. that typically brings down token cost 25-40% and improves throughput.
[03:02] Mark Liu: safe to assume we can test quantization on a dev cluster first? we have limited GPUs in prod.
[03:08] Priya Desai: yes we can run quantized variants in dev; performance profiles are in the model catalog. we'll provide recommended config and a couple of small scripts to automate the quant test.
[03:20] Aisha Khan: timeline wise we want a clear run next week and a short executive summary for our infra team.
[03:27] Luis Martinez: sounds good. for the bench run we'll aim for Wed 10/27 10am PT, that's tentative until peering and KMS are done. Priya and I will own the run from Redwood side.
[03:41] Sophie Turner: on sample data — we can provide 500 prompts and 10k anonymized records, but need to confirm anonymization is sufficient.
[03:50] Hannah Cole: we have a data handling section in the security pack, i'll flag how we handle logs and payload retention. we don't persist customer PII in logs by default, and we can redact on ingestion.
[04:05] Tom Reyes: do you support region pinning? our data residency needs APAC staging for a subset of records.
[04:12] Priya Desai: yes region pinning supported on Dedicated and Private. for hosted we can route by policy, but Dedicated will give you the isolation you want.
[04:22] Aisha Khan: cost question — if we go Dedicated later what's the commit size we should expect?
[04:27] Luis Martinez: we'll share a rough ballpark in the email but typical reserved capacity starts at monthly commitments that roughly map to the GPU pool size; we'll include a few scenarios.
[04:37] Mark Liu: any known issues with the KV cache and session long-running chats? we had some problems in an earlier open-source runtime where cache invalidation caused stale output.
[04:48] Priya Desai: our runtime handles KV cache explicitly and has TTLs; for long sessions we recommend checkpointing at 10k token intervals and using a rolling KV snapshot. we'll include best practices.
[05:05] Aisha Khan: are there any SOC2 attachments we can share internally?
[05:10] Luis Martinez: yes — SOC2 reports, penetration test summary, and our data processing addendum. i will attach them to the follow-up email along with the infra checklist.
[05:20] Sophie Turner: can Redwood run a controlled throughput run with variable batch sizes so we can decide latency vs cost tradeoffs empirically?
[05:28] Priya Desai: absolutely — we usually sweep batch sizes (1,2,4,8) and quantization levels and measure p50/p95 and tokens/sec. we'll include a spreadsheet with cost estimates per config.
[05:40] Tom Reyes: ok next step for us: finalize peering CIDR and open KMS ticket. I'll be the owner for peering.
[05:48] Mark Liu: i'll make that ticket today and update you.
[05:52] Luis Martinez: perfect. i'll send the email with links to the security pack, the quant/benchmark scripts, and a suggested schedule. we'll tentatively book Wed 10/27 10am PT and will confirm once we see peering + KMS in place.
[06:10] Aisha Khan: thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
[06:15] Luis Martinez: thanks all, we'll follow up.

Action recap (spoken):
- Redwood: send SOC2/security pack, infra checklist, sample IAM policy, and measurement scripts.
- NexaHealth: finalize VPC peering, grant KMS access, provide sample prompts and anonymized records.

Links referenced: Deck: https://redwood.example.com/deck/poc-nexa (redwood internal), Security pack: https://redwood.example.com/sec/soc2 (link), Benchmark scripts repo: https://git.redwood.example.com/poc-bench (internal), Cost sheet: https://sheets.example.com/redwood-cost-estimate (shared).

End of transcript.
